Apple's September keynote is just weeks away, but according to all reports, one key product will be missing: the standard iPhone 18. Here's when it's expected to launch instead.

Standard iPhone 18 Delayed To Early 2027 As Apple Reshuffles Release Schedule

The iPhone event is Apple's most important product launch of the year. Investors get very nervous if the company fails to deliver a new flagship iPhone. That's one reason Apple has stuck to a predictable iPhone release pattern.

Except for 2020, the event takes place every September, early in the month. Typically, the new iPhone lineup includes a standard model, two Pro models, and a fourth option like an iPhone Air.

But according to many reports that surfaced as early as May 2025, there will be no standard iPhone 18 next month.

This is a very surprising move. But so many sources have corroborated it by now that it would be more surprising if the standard iPhone 18 did appear after all.

Why no iPhone 18 at this year's September event?

We don't know for certain, but possible reasons include:

  • Apple is strategically spacing out iPhone releases to accommodate more models, such as the iPhone Ultra this year.
  • An anticipated memory crunch is expected to force Apple to adjust earlier to avoid serious supply shortages.

Regardless of the reason, the iPhone 18's absence next month is not a cancellation. The standard iPhone 18 is still coming — just delayed to early 2027.

Rumor has it three models will launch next month: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra.

Then three more will follow in early 2027: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2.

The timing will likely be no later than March. For reference, Apple launched the iPhone 16e in February and the iPhone 17e in March.

So if you want to buy Apple's newest iPhone but don't want to pay the premium for Pro or Ultra models, you'll just need to wait a few more months.

What do you think of Apple's rumored major shake-up to its iPhone release strategy? Let us know in the comments.
